content: Magnesium oxide is a medication that serves multiple purposes. Magnesium is an essential element required for normal bodily functions. Magnesium oxide can be used as an antacid to alleviate symptoms such as heartburn, sour stomach, or acid indigestion. It may also be used as a laxative for short-term, rapid bowel evacuation, such as before surgery. However, it should not be used repeatedly for this purpose. Additionally, magnesium oxide can be taken as a dietary supplement when dietary magnesium intake is insufficient. This medication is available over the counter, but it may also be prescribed for other uses. Consult your doctor or pharmacist for more information. Magnesium oxide is available in tablet and capsule forms for oral administration. The dosage typically ranges from one to four times daily, depending on the brand and the condition being treated. Follow the instructions on the package or prescription label carefully, and ask your doctor or pharmacist if you have any questions. Take magnesium oxide exactly as directed. Do not take more or less than prescribed, and do not take it more frequently than instructed. If you are taking other medications, ensure that you take them at least two hours apart from magnesium oxide. When using magnesium oxide as a laxative, take it with a full glass (8 ounces) of cold water or fruit juice. Avoid taking a dose late in the day on an empty stomach. Do not use magnesium oxide as an antacid for more than two weeks or as a laxative for more than one week unless directed by your doctor. Before taking magnesium oxide, inform your doctor and pharmacist if you are allergic to magnesium oxide, other antacids or laxatives, or any other medications. Provide a list of all prescription and nonprescription medications you are taking, especially other antacids or laxatives, anticoagulants (such as warfarin), aspirin, diuretics, ulcer medications, and vitamins. Notify your doctor if you have or have ever had heart, kidney, liver, or intestinal disease, or high blood pressure. If you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding, inform your doctor. If you become pregnant while taking magnesium oxide, contact your doctor immediately. Additionally, let your doctor know if you are on a low-salt, low-sugar, or other special diet. If you are taking magnesium oxide on a regular schedule and miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. However, if it is almost time for your next dose, skip the missed dose and continue with your regular dosing schedule. Do not take a double dose to make up for a missed one. Magnesium oxide may cause side effects. To avoid an unpleasant taste, take the tablet with citrus fruit juice or a carbonated citrus drink. Common minor side effects include cramping and diarrhea. If these symptoms are severe or persistent, inform your doctor. Serious side effects, which require immediate medical attention, include rash or hives, itching, dizziness or lightheadedness, mood or mental changes, unusual tiredness, weakness, upset stomach, or vomiting. If you experience a serious side effect, you or your doctor can report it to the FDA’s MedWatch Adverse Event Reporting program online or by phone. Store magnesium oxide in its original container, tightly closed, and out of reach of children. Keep it at room temperature, away from excessive heat and moisture (do not store it in the bathroom). Dispose of any expired or no longer needed medication properly. Consult your pharmacist for guidance on proper disposal. In case of an overdose, contact your local poison control center at 1-800-222-1222. If the individual has collapsed or is not breathing, call emergency services at 911. If this medication has been prescribed for you, keep all appointments with your doctor to monitor your response to magnesium oxide. Do not share your medication with others.
